title: A Chance in a Million
question: What was the chance in a million?

meanings.usage: 形容人容易相信不真实的事物
指两件或多件事情同时发生但没有明显关联
形容不太可能发生的事
修饰动词，表示以邪恶的方式
指使分离的人或物再次聚在一起
指未证实的情况下认为某事是真实的
指将原本在一起的东西分开
表达对某人或某事的藐视

examples.en: A novelist would bring his story to a conclusion by presenting coincidences.
examples.zh: 小说家会通过呈现一系列巧合来给故事收尾。

examples.en: Franz poured scorn on the idea.
examples.zh: 弗朗茨对这个想法嗤之以鼻。

examples.en: Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story.
examples.zh: 布斯曼太太对这件事非常了解。

phrases.usage: 极小的可能性，万分之一的可能

examples.en: There was a chance in a million that she might be right.
examples.zh: 她可能是对的，这种可能性微乎其微。

examples.en: Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
examples.zh: 汉斯解释了他是如何活下来的。

examples.en: Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.
examples.zh: 汉斯步行回到了西德。

examples.en: Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away.
examples.zh: 汉斯在五十英里外的一个村庄定居下来。

examples.en: He was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
examples.zh: 人们以为他二十年前就已经死了。

examples.en: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences.
examples.zh: 然而，在现实生活中，情况有时确实会凑巧带来巧合。

examples.en: He really was Franz's long-lost brother.
examples.zh: 他确实是弗朗茨失散多年的兄弟。

sentences.en: We are less credulous than we used to be.
sentences.zh: 我们不像以前那样轻信了。

sentences.en: In the nineteenth century, a novelist would bring his story to a conclusion
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，小说家在故事的结尾

sentences.en: by presenting his readers with a series of coincidences--most of them wildly improbable.
sentences.zh: 会给读者安排一连串的巧合——其中大部分都是极不可能发生的。

sentences.en: Readers happily accepted the fact that an obscure maidservant was really the hero's mother.
sentences.zh: 读者们欣然接受一个默默无闻的女仆竟然是主人公的母亲这一事实。

sentences.en: A long-lost brother, who was presumed dead, was really alive all the time
sentences.zh: 一个被认为已死去的失散多年的兄弟，实际上一直活着，

sentences.en: and wickedly plotting to bring about the hero's downfall. And so on.
sentences.zh: 并且阴险地策划着让主人公垮台。诸如此类。

sentences.en: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 现代读者会觉得这种天真的结局完全不能接受。

sentences.en: Yet, in real life, circumstances do sometimes conspire to bring about coincidences which anyone but a nineteenth century novelist would find incredible.
sentences.zh: 然而，在现实生活中，情况有时确实会凑巧地导致巧合的发生，除了19世纪的小说家，其他任何人都觉得不可思议。

sentences.en: When I was a boy, my grandfather told me how a German taxi driver, Franz Bussman,
sentences.zh: 我小时候，祖父给我讲了一个德国出租车司机弗朗兹·布斯曼的故事，

sentences.en: found a brother who was thought to have been killed twenty years before.
sentences.zh: 他找到了一个被认为在20年前阵亡的兄弟。

sentences.en: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
sentences.zh: 在和妻子徒步旅行时，他停下来和一名工人交谈。

sentences.en: After they had gone on, Mrs. Bussman commented on the workman's close resemblance to her husband
sentences.zh: 他们继续前行后，布斯曼夫人评论说那个工人长得很像她丈夫，

sentences.en: and even suggested that he might be his brother.
sentences.zh: 甚至猜测他可能是她丈夫的兄弟。

sentences.en: Franz poured scorn on the idea,
sentences.zh: 弗朗兹对这个想法嗤之以鼻，

sentences.en: pointing out that his brother had been killed in action during the war.
sentences.zh: 指出他兄弟在战争中阵亡了。

sentences.en: Though Mrs. Bussman was fully acquainted with this story,
sentences.zh: 尽管布斯曼夫人完全了解这个故事，

sentences.en: she thought that there was a chance in a million that she might be right.
sentences.zh: 她觉得她有可能说对了，尽管几率是百万分之一。

sentences.en: A few days later, she sent a boy to the workman to ask him if his name was Hans Bussman.
sentences.zh: 几天后，她派了一个男孩去问那个工人，他是否叫汉斯·布斯曼。

sentences.en: Needless to say, the man's name was Hans Bussman and he really was Franz's long-lost brother.
sentences.zh: 不用说，那个人的名字就是汉斯·布斯曼，他确实是弗朗兹失散多年的兄弟。

sentences.en: When the brothers were reunited,
sentences.zh: 兄弟俩团聚后，

sentences.en: Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
sentences.zh: 汉斯解释了他为什么还活着。

sentences.en: After having been wounded towards the end of the war,
sentences.zh: 在战争快结束时受伤后，

sentences.en: he had been sent to hospital and was separated from his unit.
sentences.zh: 他被送往医院，与部队失散了。

sentences.en: The hospital had been bombed and Hans had made his way back into Western Germany on foot.
sentences.zh: 医院被轰炸了，汉斯徒步回到了西德。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, his unit was lost and all records of him had been destroyed.
sentences.zh: 同时，他的部队失散了，所有关于他的记录都被销毁了。

sentences.en: Hans returned to his family home, but the house had been bombed
sentences.zh: 汉斯回到了他的老家，但是房子被炸毁了，

sentences.en: and no one in the neighbourhood knew what had become of the inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 邻居们也不知道住户们怎么样了。

sentences.en: Assuming that his family had been killed during an air raid,
sentences.zh: 以为他的家人在空袭中丧生，

sentences.en: Hans settled down in a village fifty miles away where he had remained ever since.
sentences.zh: 汉斯在一个五十英里外的小村庄安顿下来，自此一直住在那里。

grammar.title: 过去完成时 (Past Perfect Tense)
grammar.definition: 表示在过去某一时刻之前已经完成的动作，常用于描述过去的过去发生的事
grammar.usage: 用于叙述过去事件时，表示先发生的动作，常与一般过去时连用

examples.en: He had been wounded towards the end of the war.
examples.zh: 他在战争末期受了伤。

examples.en: The hospital had been bombed and all records had been destroyed.
examples.zh: 医院被炸毁了，所有记录都被销毁了。

grammar.title: 过去分词短语作状语
grammar.definition: 过去分词可以作状语，表示原因、时间、方式等
grammar.structure: Having + 过去分词 或 过去分词
grammar.usage: 用来简化从句，使句子更加简洁

examples.en: After having been wounded, he had been sent to hospital.
examples.zh: 受伤后，他被送进了医院。

examples.en: Assuming that his family had been killed, Hans settled down in a village.
examples.zh: 以为家人在空袭中遇难了，汉斯在一个村庄安顿下来。

grammar.title: 间接引语 (Indirect Speech) - 过去完成时的使用
grammar.definition: 在间接引语中，如果引用的动作发生在主句动作之前，且时间已过，需用过去完成时
grammar.structure: 主句动词 + that + 主语 + had + 过去分词
grammar.usage: 用于转述别人说过的话，且所转述的内容在转述之前就已发生

examples.en: Hans explained how it was that he was still alive.
examples.zh: 汉斯解释了他是如何活下来的。

examples.en: She thought there was a chance she might be right.
examples.zh: 她认为她可能是对的。

patterns.pattern: While + doing..., 主语 + 动词...

original.en: While on a walking tour with his wife, he stopped to talk to a workman.
original.zh: 在和妻子徒步旅行时，他停下来和一个工人聊天。

examples.en: While waiting for the bus, she read a book.
examples.zh: 等公交车时，她读了一本书。

examples.en: While traveling in Europe, they visited many museums.
examples.zh: 在欧洲旅行时，他们参观了很多博物馆。

original.en: Needless to say, the man's name was Hans Bussman.
original.zh: 不用说，这个人的名字就是汉斯·布斯曼。

examples.en: Needless to say, he passed the exam easily.
examples.zh: 不用说，他轻松地通过了考试。

examples.en: Needless to say, she was very happy about the news.
examples.zh: 不用说，她对这个消息非常高兴。

original.en: Modern readers would find such naive solutions totally unacceptable.
original.zh: 现代读者会觉得这种幼稚的解决方法完全不可接受。

examples.en: I find it incredible that such coincidences happen.
examples.zh: 我觉得这样的巧合发生真是令人难以置信。

examples.en: They consider it possible that he survived the war.
examples.zh: 他们认为他在战争中存活下来是可能的。

patterns.pattern: 主语 + suggested that + 主语 + might be / might have been

original.en: She even suggested that he might be his brother.
original.zh: 她甚至猜测他可能是他的兄弟。

examples.en: The doctor suggested that she might be allergic to something.
examples.zh: 医生说她可能对什么东西过敏。

examples.en: He suggested that the letter might have been lost.
examples.zh: 他猜测那封信可能丢了。
